A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTA survival-analysis study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite extensive rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original survival-prediction experiments on five TCGA cohorts, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and risk-stratification and prototype visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, sensitivity settings, and detailed prototype-based case analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the specified weighting procedure: v2 scales the retained transport plan by Ntot and row-normalizes both the softmax–transport mixture and the pseudo-labels; v1's equations use them directly. These are localized changes to the method as written. The architecture remains the same, and the PDFs do not establish whether implementation or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five TCGA cohorts—BRCA, BLCA, STAD, CRC, and KIRC—for paired histopathology/genomics disease-specific survival prediction. The additional BRCA cases and sensitivity experiments remain within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds MRePath to the evaluated comparators in Table 1; v1 only discusses and cites it. Other main-table comparators and the ResNet50 comparison set are retained. KMeans and alternative OT assignments already appeared in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: v2 adds sensitivity settings using batch size 16, two refiner layers, and a linear transport-mass schedule (Tables 5 and 10). Cohort sizes, five-fold site-stratified evaluation, metrics, and default training settings remain unchanged. The existing H=0 result row is relabeled H=1 (single-head), with identical scores, rather than providing evidence of a new run.

E4.justification: v2 extends sensitivity testing to batch size, refiner depth, and curriculum-schedule variants. Appendix D replaces the older single-slide heatmaps and pathway-count displays with two BRCA cases linking prototype heatmaps, representative patches, and hallmark pathways. Most component ablations and parameter sweeps were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean±standard deviation with five-fold evaluation and Kaplan–Meier confidence regions with log-rank tests. v2 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence-interval methods, or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: New results include MRePath's overall C-index of 0.663 and averages of 0.673, 0.690, and 0.687 for batch size 16, two refiner layers, and linear scheduling. Retained numerical results—including TTA's 0.693 main average, 0.677 ResNet50 average, and log-rank p-values—are unchanged. Appendix D supplies new case-specific qualitative findings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the abstract alignment-minus-distinctiveness formulation with an explicit anchor margin, a logistic-loss interpretation, and gradient decomposition. v2 also corrects Algorithm 1's scaling-vector dimension and makes main-text Eq. 8 match the partial-mass constraints already in v1's appendix. The principal OT derivations and equivalence proof remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: v1 presents a unified min–max optimization formulation and a new theoretical perspective as central contributions. v2 withdraws that explicit formulation claim and centers the contribution on a representation-learning principle that balances alignment and distinctiveness, emphasizing over-alignment and interpretable clinical associations. This substantively revises the claimed conceptual contribution while retaining the performance claim.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the competing-forces interpretation with a detailed account of complementary assignment-level alignment and geometric anchor separation. Appendix A.1 explains why statistical independence and identical patient representations are unnecessary. Appendices C–D add cohort-specific mechanism interpretations and explicitly qualify pathway associations as noncausal, substantially expanding the scientific interpretation and its boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents padding masks, shared prototypes across heads, matched comparator inputs, and a common configuration across folds and cohorts. Code changes from promised availability to reported availability. Conversely, v1's RTX 4090 hardware statement and explicit two-random-subset consistency description disappear. Most configuration values are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds a more explicit distinction between TTA's joint concatenated-token transport plan and MOTCat/MMP. The bibliography adds several works, including CSRv2 and Beyond Matryoshka, while removing background references such as Multimodal Biomedical AI and DINOv2. The principal survival-analysis literature and competing-method positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, conclusion, and substantial appendix discussion are extensively rewritten. Min–max terminology is replaced, experimental material receives additional subsection structure, and the appendices become a separately introduced supplement with a contents list. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: The two-column document becomes a single-column paper with a separately numbered supplement, extensively resizing and relocating displays. v2 adds a consolidated robustness chart and assignment table, partly redisplaying existing appendix results. Older pathway-count and full-prototype heatmap panels are replaced by detailed two-case visual composites.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity through a more defensible joint-objective framing, corrected mathematical details, a relevant additional comparator, targeted sensitivity checks, and more informative tissue–pathway visualizations. The principal performance evidence is unchanged. Benefits are tempered by lost hardware and consistency-training details and inconsistent temperature scaling in the new margin formulation between Eq. 18 and Appendix A.1. Overall, the changes provide a limited net improvement in explanation and evidential support.
